hook: Lemon juice, vinegar and stomach acid all hand out the same thing: hydrogen ions, which are bare protons. Baking soda, ammonia and soap take them in. Seeing an acid-base reaction as a single proton moving from one particle to another explains reactions that the old "acids have H, bases have OH" rule cannot.

prereq.q: What is left when a hydrogen atom loses its electron?
prereq.why: A hydrogen atom is one proton and one electron, so H⁺ is just a proton.

prereq.q: Which part of a water molecule carries a partial negative charge and lone pairs?
prereq.why: Oxygen is more electronegative and has two lone pairs.

prereq.q: In H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l), what kind of reaction is shown?
prereq.why: An H⁺ moves to OH⁻ to form water.

figure.caption: A proton transfer. HF gives an H⁺ to a water molecule. Each reactant and the product it becomes form a conjugate pair, differing by one H⁺.

chain.cause: A Brønsted-Lowry acid gives up an H⁺ (a proton)
chain.effect: what remains is its conjugate base, with one less H and one less + charge

chain.cause: A Brønsted-Lowry base uses a lone pair to accept the H⁺
chain.effect: it becomes its conjugate acid, with one more H and one more + charge

chain.cause: Water has both O–H bonds and lone pairs on oxygen
chain.effect: it can act as an acid or a base: it is amphoteric

chain.cause: A bare proton bonds at once to a water molecule
chain.effect: acid in water gives hydronium ions, H₃O⁺

ideas: A Brønsted-Lowry acid is a proton donor; a Brønsted-Lowry base is a proton acceptor (it needs a lone pair).
A conjugate acid-base pair differs by exactly one H⁺: HF/F⁻, NH₄⁺/NH₃, H₂O/OH⁻, H₃O⁺/H₂O.
Amphoteric species such as H₂O and HCO₃⁻ can donate or accept a proton.
In water, H⁺ is carried as hydronium, H₃O⁺. Neutralization: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O.

misconception.wrong: An acid is anything with H in its formula, and a base is anything with OH.
misconception.right: Acid and base describe what a particle does in a reaction. Methane has H but gives up no protons; ammonia has no OH but accepts a proton. Look for the H⁺ that moves.

summary: In a Brønsted-Lowry acid-base reaction, a proton (H⁺) moves from the acid to the base. The acid becomes its conjugate base and the base becomes its conjugate acid; each pair differs by one H⁺. Water is amphoteric, and in water a proton is carried as hydronium, H₃O⁺.
